description.value: Major not-for-profit art gallery founded in 1931, housed in a landmark building in downtown Vancouver. Known for its extensive Emily Carr collection and rotating international exhibitions. A natural rest stop for cyclists on the downtown seawall loop, with on-site dining and a gallery shop.

bike_parking_detail: 7 racks within 100m: stands (12 spaces) at 44m; stands (2 spaces) at 70m; stands (2 spaces) at 77m; stands (6 spaces) at 82m; stands (2 spaces) at 83m; stands (2 spaces) at 85m; stands (2 spaces) at 89m. Total: 28 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the gallery is open and active with 2026 exhibitions and summer hours. The address is confirmed on both OSM and the website footer. The navigation menu includes 'Dine' under the Visit section, confirming food is available on site. No mention of bike parking, water refill, washrooms, Wi-Fi, or other cyclist-specific amenities appears in the website content or OSM tags. OSM confirms wheelchair accessibility but has no bike-related tags.
concerns: Gallery is cashless — debit/credit only, no Apple Pay or Google Pay accepted
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Major cultural attraction in downtown Vancouver, directly accessible by bike on well-known cycling routes. On-site dining and shop make it a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists.

Café or food on site.detail: 'Dine' listed as a visitor option under the Visit section of the main navigation

wow_evidence: One of Canada's major art museums — landmark Rattenbury courthouse building, definitive Emily Carr collection, international blockbuster exhibitions; national/international band. Visit is strong but less singular than MOA (delight 2 vs 3).
blurb: Canada's major western art museum; Emily Carr collection in a landmark former courthouse.
